author: n. a. sauceda
title: Nosek returns as Panthers visit Devils amid playoff push - Central Broward News
text:
Tomas Nosek is set to make his season debut for the Florida Panthers on Tuesday as they face the New Jersey Devils at Prudential Center. Nosek, who had offseason surgery, has not played yet this season but contributed in 16 playoff games last year during the Panthers’ second consecutive Stanley Cup run. The 33-year-old will center the fourth line in his return.
“I want them to have a little bit of fun,” said Panthers head coach Paul Maurice about Nosek and Dmitry Kulikov, who also recently returned from injury. “I give both of them credit. They worked so hard to get back. It was not easy on them. I want them to get out there and feel good because we certainly feel good having them back in our lineup.”
The Panthers are currently 30-27-3 and sit eight points behind the second wild-card spot in the Eastern Conference after losing two of their first three games following the break. In their most recent game, Florida lost 5-4 to the New York Islanders after conceding a goal in the final minute.
Matthew Tkachuk registered three assists in that loss, while Sam Bennett scored twice, extending his point streak to three games. Sam Reinhart tied the game late with less than two minutes remaining.
“Very tough ending the last game,” Tkachuk said. “Tough time of the year for a game like that to happen. Just got to turn the page. This is a big week. We want to try and put ourselves in somewhat of a conversation to get back. It’s a daunting task, but most importantly it’s just getting back to our game.”
Uvis Balinskis returns from an undisclosed injury for Florida, while Donovon Sebrango and Jeff Petry will be scratched from tonight’s lineup. Tobias Bjornfot is expected to play after being out since February 4th.
Sergei Bobrovsky will start as goaltender for Florida.
The Devils are seventh in their division with a record of 29-29-2 and recently ended a five-game losing streak by defeating St. Louis 3-1 on Saturday. Jacob Markstrom stopped 25 shots in that win and is expected to start against Florida tonight.
Nico Hischier and Jesper Bratt lead New Jersey with 43 assists each this season, while Jack Hughes has collected 39 points since returning from Olympic play with Team USA.
This marks the third meeting between these teams this season; each has won once at home so far.
“They’re dynamic,” Maurice said about New Jersey’s roster. “They’ve got some really fast, really skilled players. They play that fast game… What we need to do tonight is not just for the New Jersey Devils. We need to get our game back to where we like it, to look the way we like.”
Additional comments from players reflect their focus on taking things one step at a time:
“Don’t try to get it all back in one shift. Keep your shifts short, keep your game as simple as you possibly can. Enjoy it…” – Paul Maurice on Tomas Nosek’s return
“Just play this one game. Just play this style that we’ve been playing for three-plus years…” – Matthew Tkachuk
“We know what the situation is… We just look at one game at a time and not too much further ahead or behind.” – Anton Lundell
Notable team statistics include Aaron Ekblad recording four multi-assist games this season; Mackie Samoskevich leading with +13 penalty drawn rating; Sam Reinhart tying Olli Jokinen for third-most goals in franchise history; Anton Lundell winning over half his faceoffs; and Sam Bennett nearing his 200th NHL assist milestone.
Florida recently loaned forward Luke Kunin to Charlotte (AHL).
The match will be broadcast Tuesday night via Scripps Sports, Panthers Plus, TNT, HBO Max, local radio stations including WQAM-AM (Dade/Broward), WESP-FM (Palm Beach), WCTH (Florida Keys), WCZR (Treasure Coast), as well as through streaming apps.
